free_tier.stated: 10 GiB storage AND 10 GiB/month bandwidth on GitHub Free (also 10/10 on Pro and Free-for-orgs; 250 GiB each on Team/Enterprise Cloud). This is UP from the old 1 GiB/1 GiB. The docs now show a 10 GiB table. Pre-paid data packs are gone; it is metered with a budget setting.

retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Metered but included up to 10 GiB/month. Over quota with no payment method, 'Git LFS support is disabled on your account until the next month'. With a $0 budget, usage is blocked for the rest of the calendar month. No free CDN in front of LFS.

tooling: git-lfs (git-lfs/git-lfs, ~10k stars). git-annex can also use GitHub LFS as a special-remote backend (see the git-lfs remote entry). REST API for repo management.
chaining: 10 GiB per account x unlimited free accounts. Note the ownership trick in GitHub's own docs: 'Anyone with write access to a repository can push files to Git LFS without increasing their personal bandwidth and storage use'. Usage lands on the REPO OWNER. So a collaborator-heavy layout concentrates the bill on one account, which is the opposite of what you want; the shardable axis is accounts-as-repo-owners.
limits_note: Per-file: 2 GB on Free/Pro, 4 GB on Team, 5 GB on Enterprise Cloud. Storage is billed on all LFS objects ever associated with a repo, hourly-averaged, and 'If you delete Git LFS objects partway through a calendar month, the storage usage for that month is not recalculated'. Re-pushing a 1-byte change to a 500 MB file consumes another 500 MB. Actions pulling LFS counts against the repo owner's bandwidth.
